rationale.validation: Accurately distinguishes grammar acceptance from security and Python semantics. Visible calls establish ignored allow_variables, power syntax, real 15/1024 outputs and null domain results. No claim generated Python was executed.
rationale.guidance: Concrete AST allowlist, no eval/exec, input length/depth/exponent limits, generic-error/logging/rate-limit recommendations and OWASP mapping.
rationale.implementation_consistency: Static counterexample: compute("10.0 ** 1000") permits exponent1000 and reaches operator.pow, which overflows; wrapper only catches UnsafeExpression/ZeroDivisionError, contradicting same generic error for all failures and overflow handling. Repeated permitted powers also have no intermediate integer-size bound, so the drop-in safe/DoS assurance is unsupported. Benign listed arithmetic and malicious syntax rejection are otherwise represented.
